ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137/r5.claim: They lose their souls by trading worship of God for idols; “souls” implies lost comfort or happiness, since their persons remain punished. Their fabricated gods and expected intercession fail them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137/r5.anchor: كونهم اشتروا عبادة الآلهة بعبادة الله تعالى، فخسروا في تجارتهم خسرانا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r1.claim: Those who lost themselves cheated themselves.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r1.anchor: عن السدى في قوله عز وجل : اولئك الذي خسروا انفسهم قال غبنوا انفسهم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r2.claim: What went astray from them did so on the Day of Resurrection.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قوله : وضل عنهم قال في القيامة

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r3.claim: What they invented means what they used to lie about in worldly life.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r3.anchor: وبه عن ابن عباس ماكانوا يفترون : ماكانوا يكذبون في الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r4.claim: Alternatively, what they invented means their association of partners with God.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : ماكانوا يفترون اي يشركون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r1.claim: Losing their selves means deserving punishment; no loss is greater than losing oneself, and what they hoped their fabrications would bring has disappeared from them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r1.anchor:
خسروا أنفسهم
بوجوب العذاب عليهم، ولا خسران أعظم من خسران النفس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r2.claim: Ḍalla means it was lost or perished and was not found where they had hoped.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r2.anchor:
وضل
معناه:
تلف ولم يجدوه حيث أملوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p314#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p314#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p314#2/r1.claim: The deniers lose themselves in blazing Hell and their invented gods disappear, failing to help and instead harming them; other verses show their former idols disowning them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r1.claim: A poetic example glosses the verb جرمت as what the hands earned or committed.

MUQATIL:11:19-21/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:19-21/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:19-21/r2.claim: They have cheated themselves of salvation, and the objects they fabricated as gods have disappeared.
MUQATIL:11:19-21/r2.anchor: يعنى بسابقى الله { في الأرض } هربا حتى يجزيهم بأعمالهم الخبيثة،

NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#3/r1.claim: They lose themselves by exchanging worship of God for worship of idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم ﴾ حيث اشتروا عبادة الآلهة بعبادة الله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#3/r2.claim: Their fabricated gods and supposed intercessors disappear, leaving them with nothing they had imagined.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ وضل عنهم ﴾ وبطل عنهم وضاع ما اشتروه وهو ﴿ ما كانوا يفترون ﴾ من الآلهة وشفاعتها

QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r1.claim: The clause is a nominal sentence whose subject is “those” and predicate is “the ones who lost themselves”; what they fabricated has disappeared and been lost.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r1.anchor: ابتداء وخبر. { وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون }

RAZI-FULL:v17p166/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p166/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p166/r5.claim: They lose themselves by exchanging worship of God for worship of idols, the greatest kind of loss.
RAZI-FULL:v17p166/r5.anchor: اشتروا عبادة الآلهة بعبادة الله تعالى فكان هذا الخسران أعظم وجوه الخسران

RAZI-FULL:v17p166/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p166/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p166/r6.claim: Their fabricated gods and claims vanish: they traded the noble religion for a base worldly gain that itself perishes, completing their loss in this life and the next.
RAZI-FULL:v17p166/r6.anchor: لأنهم أعطوا الشريف ، ورضوا بأخذ الخسيس ، وهذا عين الخسران في الدنيا ثم في الآخرة

STUDYQURAN:11:20/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:20/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:20/r5.claim: What the disbelievers fabricated, including idols, ideas, and religious beliefs, will ultimately forsake them.
STUDYQURAN:11:20/r5.anchor: one will ultimately be forsaken by what one has fabricated, including false idols, ideas, and religious beliefs

TAB-FULL:v12p373/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p373/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p373/r1.claim: These people lose their share of God’s mercy; their fabricated claims and supposed partners fail them, taking a different path that leads to Hell or, if a claimed deity is God’s ally, Paradise rather than their path.
TAB-FULL:v12p373/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: هؤلاء الذين هذه صفتهم، هم الذين غبنوا أنفسهم حظوظها من رحمة الله.

TAB-FULL:v12p373/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p373/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p373/r2.claim: The false gods prove nonexistent as deities: in this world they were stones, wood, or copper, and they no longer accompany their worshippers.
TAB-FULL:v12p373/r2.anchor: وصارت آلهتهم عدما لا شيء، لأنها كانت في الدنيا حجارة أو خشبا أو نحاسا،

TABATABAI:11:20-21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:20-21/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:20-21/r6.claim: Losing one’s self is a metaphor: God entrusted each person with himself, and disbelief and sin squander that entrusted self.

TABATABAI:11:20-21/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:20-21/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:20-21/r7.claim: Their fabricated deities and claims are imaginary; with worldly life ended, these inventions disappear and the truth becomes manifest.
TABATABAI:11:20-21/r7.anchor: وبانطواء بساط الحياة الدنيا يزول وينمحي تلك الأوهام

TABRISI:11:20-22/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:20-22/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:20-22/r6.claim: They lose themselves by doing what earns punishment and destruction; loss of one’s self is the greatest loss because it has no replacement, and their fabricated gods and claims disappear.
TABRISI:11:20-22/r6.anchor: من حيث فعلوا ما استحقوا به العقاب فهلكوا فذلك خسران أنفسهم

TABRISI:11:20-22/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:20-22/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:20-22/r10.claim: The clarification about the unjust forger answers people who thought ignorance of God would not harm them: one who does not know God may also lie about Him, and none is more unjust than such a liar.
TABRISI:11:20-22/r10.anchor: أنه سبحانه أراد أن يبين حال العاقل والغافل فكأنهم قالوا وما يضرنا أن لا نعرف ذلك

ASAD-NOTES:11:21#n42/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:21#n42/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:21#n42/r1.claim: What people invent includes false divine powers and deceptive half-truths such as luck, wealth, personal power, nationalism, and materialism, which obscure spiritual values and waste their lives.
ASAD-NOTES:11:21#n42/r1.anchor: deceptive ideas and "glittering half-truths meant to delude the mind" (see 6:112 and the corresponding note)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r1.claim: Losing themselves means ending in Hell; this is the greatest loss because the self has no replacement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r1.anchor: أي صاروا إلى النار، وخسران النفس أعظم الخسران

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r2.claim: Their fabrications fail and bring no benefit in the Afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r2.anchor: بطل افتراؤهم في الدنيا فلم ينفعهم في الآخرة شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r3.claim: The idols they hoped would benefit them have disappeared.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384/r3.anchor: ذهبت عنهم الأوثان التي كانوا يؤملون بها الانتفاع

ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r1.claim: The condemned people lose themselves by exchanging worship of God for worship of idols.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r1.anchor: بإشتراء عبادة الآلهة بعبادة الله تعالى شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that they exchanged guidance for error and the afterlife for this world, losing the worldly enjoyment and authority obtained by that exchange.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : ( خسروا ) بسبب تبديلهم الهداية بالضلالة والآخرة بالدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r3.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r3.claim: Al-Baḥr supplies an omitted modifier: they lost the happiness and comfort of their souls, since the selves themselves remain tormented.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r3.anchor: وفي البحر أنه على حذف مضاف أي ( خسروا ) سعادة أنفسهم وراحتها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r4.claim: He prefers the literal wording: their continuing existence in torment is effectively their being kept in loss.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r4.anchor: وتعقب بأن إبقاءه على ظاهره أولى لأن البقاء في العذاب كالإبقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p32#2/r5.claim: What they had invented, their supposed gods and their intercession, has vanished from them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p169#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p169#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p169#2/r3.claim: They cheated themselves, and the supposed intercession they invented for angels and idols has vanished.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p169#2/r3.anchor: {أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم} غبنوا أنفسهم، {وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون}

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:21-22/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:21-22/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:21-22/r1.claim: They lose themselves by exchanging worship of God for idols; the idols and imagined intercession disappear, or the people lose what they gained and are left with regret.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:21-22/r1.anchor: باشتراء عبادة الآلهة بعبادة الله تعالى.. { وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون } من الآلهة وشفاعتها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r1.claim: They lose themselves by wasting the original disposition that readily follows good and resists evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r1.anchor: اي بتضييع الفطرة الأولى التي هي سهولة الانقياد للخير وصعوبة الانقياد للشر

BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r2.claim: Their invented gods disappear and cannot help them; whoever loses himself through claiming a partnership with his Creator is among the most lost.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r2.anchor: أي يتعمدون كذبه مما ادعوا كونهم آلهة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r4.claim: The author defines inability to thwart as being unable to prevent what God wills, doubling as an increase by an equal or larger amount, and capacity as a power by which limbs act.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r4.anchor: والإعجاز : الامتناع من المراد بما لا يمكن معه إيقاعه ؛ والمضاعفة : الزيادة على المقدار بمثله أو أكثر ؛ والاستطاعة : قوة ينطاع بها الجوارح للفعل

DURR-FULL:v4p413/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p413/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p413/r9.claim: Those who lost themselves have cheated or deprived themselves.
DURR-FULL:v4p413/r9.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه {أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم} قال: غبنوا أنفسهم
